Stock Market News for April 10, 2026 291 news published. RSS Feed Google News AI infrastructure, financing shakeups CoreWeave (CRWV) again dominated headlines with a multi-year deal with Anthropic and an upsized $3.5 billion convertible notes offering. The pact boosts demand visibility for GPU capacity; the financing sharpens the trade-off between rapid expansion and shareholder dilution, a key watch for investors assessing AI infrastructure cap-structure risk. Autonomy, robotics and drone wins Pony.ai (PONY) rolled out PonyWorld 2.0, a self-improving physical AI engine that could compress robotaxi unit costs over time. Wrap (WRAP) secured a pre-order for over 20 drone and counter-drone systems across the U.K. and Europe, highlighting rising defense and commercial demand: release. Semiconductors and tech demand cues Omdia’s report shows the global smartphone market edged up 1% in 1Q26, a positive read-through for memory and SoC suppliers: read. Silicon Motion (SIMO) scheduled its Q1 2026 call, a near-term proxy for NAND controller demand and SSD pricing trends. Quantum security and advanced tech MicroCloud Hologram Inc. (HOLO) says it combined quantum key distribution and QRNG with holographic authentication. Commercialization remains speculative, but the product taps investor interest in quantum-resistant security for telecom and defense. Arqit Quantum Inc. (ARQQ) released select preliminary financials for the first half of fiscal 2026. Watch cash runway and program spending; funding and revenue trajectories will determine the viability of its quantum encryption roadmap. Biotech catalysts and clinical readouts Allogene Therapeutics (ALLO) said it will announce an interim futility analysis from its pivotal ALPHA3 trial on April 13. That readout is a near-term binary for first-line consolidation LBCL and could swing sentiment sharply. IDEAYA Biosciences (IDYA) scheduled topline results for the Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 trial in metastatic uveal melanoma on April 13—another potential binary event for oncology investors: announcement. Mesoblast (MESO) received IND clearance to proceed directly to a registrational trial for Ryoncil® in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. That regulatory pathway accelerates potential commercialization timelines and is material for clinical-stage biotech investors. Annovis (ANVS) closed a $10 million offering, extending runway toward a planned Phase 3 Alzheimer’s submission; cash relief reduces near-term financing risk. Milestone Pharmaceuticals (MIST) launched its RESET-PSVT registry for CARDAMYST™, aiming to build real-world evidence that could affect payer discussions and commercial uptake. Energy, mining and credit moves Diamondback Energy (FANG) announced pricing of tender offers for its 4.400% 2051 and 4.250% 2052 senior notes. The swap impacts long-duration energy credit curves and shows proactive liability management in a rising-rate environment. Skeena Gold & Silver (SKE) closed a US$750 million senior secured notes offering, materially reshaping financing for its Copper Mountain project and reducing near-term refinancing uncertainty. Credit vehicles and corporate filings Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BX) filed a public registration statement with the SEC. Investors will watch the vehicle’s capital plan for data-center and digital infrastructure exposure. Trinity Capital (TRIN) reported $395 million of new commitments and $306 million funded in 1Q26, signaling continued deal flow in venture lending. Auto sector filings and production updates Li Auto (LI) filed its Form 20-F, adding clarity on China sales and supply-chain notes ahead of the seasonally important selling cycle. NIO (NIO) also filed its annual report on Form 20-F, an important disclosure checkpoint for investors tracking China EV demand. Aura (AUGO) posted preliminary Q1 production records, suggesting margin recovery is possible if sales catch up with output.
